tasks.title: A moon is orbiting a planet
tasks.statement:
A moon is orbiting a planet such that the plane of its orbit is perpendicular to the surface of the planet where an observer is standing. After some necessary scaling, suppose the orbit satisfies the following equation:

9(x*sqrt(3)y / 2 + ... )

Consider Cartesian coordinates where x is on the horizontal plane and y is on the zenith of the observer. Let r be the radius of the moon. Assume that the period of rotation of the planet is much larger than the orbital period of the moon. Ignore the atmospheric refraction.

parts.question: Calculate the semimajor and semiminor axis of the ellipse.
parts.reference: Rewrite the orbit equation using polar coordinate or simplify by introducing new variables x* and y*. Determine semi major and semi minor axis of the orbit. Semi major axis is 5, semi minor axis is 3.

parts.question: Calculate the zenith angle of perigee.
parts.reference: At the perigee, alpha - pi/3 = pi. Thus, the zenith angle at the perigee is 5pi/6.

parts.question: Determine tan(theta / 2) where theta is the elevation angle (altitude of the upper tangent of the moon) when the moon looks largest to the observer.
parts.reference: Characterize the coordinates of the moon when it looks largest (y0 = r). Rewrite the equation as a quadratic equation in x0, solve for x0 and choose the smaller one. Find tan(theta/2) = r / x0 = 21r / (4r*sqrt(3) + 18 - 15*sqrt(-r^2 + 4r*sqrt(3) + 9)).

tasks.title: Two massive stars A and B
tasks.statement: Two massive stars A and B with masses m_A and m_B are separated by a distance d. Both stars orbit around their center of mass under gravitational force. Assume their orbits are circular and lie on the X-Y plane whose origin is at the stars’ center of mass (see Figure 2). An observer standing on the Y-Z plane sees the stars from a large distance with an angle theta relatively to the Z-axis. He measures that the velocity component of star A to his line of sight has the form K cos(omega t + epsilon), where K and epsilon are positive. Assume that the observer then identifies that star A has mass equal to 30 M_S where M_S is the Sun’s mass. In addition, he observes that star B produces X-rays and then realizes that it could be a neutron star or a black hole. This conclusion would depend on m_B, i.e.: i) If m_B < 2 M_S, then B is a neutron star; ii) If m_B > 2 M_S, then B is a black hole.

parts.question: Find the expressions for the tangential and angular speeds of star A.
parts.reference: The center of gravity of the stars relative to star A is given by r_A = m_B / (m_A + m_B) * d. Using gravitational force and circular orbit equation, find v_A = m_B * sqrt(G / ((m_A + m_B) * d)) and omega = sqrt(G(m_A + m_B) / d^3).

parts.question: Express K^3 / (omega G) in terms of m_A, m_B, and theta where G is the universal gravitational constant.
parts.reference: In Cartesian coordinate system, velocity of A is v_A(t). Project onto observer line of sight r_hat_P = cos(theta) k_hat + sin(theta) j_hat. K = v_A sin(theta). Express K^3 / (omega G) = m_B^3 / (m_A + m_B)^2 * sin^3(theta).

parts.question: A measurement by the observer shows that K^3 / (omega G) = 1 / 250 M_S. In practice, the value of theta is usually not known. What is the condition on theta for star B to be a black hole?
parts.reference: From previous result, sin^3(theta) < 64 / 125, so sin(theta) < 0.8. Since theta in [0, pi], theta is less than 53 degrees or greater than 127 degrees.

tasks.title: Suppose a static spherical star consists of N neutral particles
tasks.statement: Suppose a static spherical star consists of N neutral particles with radius R (see Figure 3) with 0 <= theta <= pi, 0 <= phi <= 2pi, satisfying the given equation of states P V = N k ln(T_R / T_0). Assume that T_R <= T_0. Suppose the star undergoes a quasi-static process, in which it may slightly contract or expand. The star satisfies first law of thermodynamics Q = Delta M c^2 + W. Assume T_0 to be constant, while T_R variable.

parts.question: Simplify the stellar equation of state (1) if Delta T = T_R - T_0 approx 0 (this is called ideal star)
parts.reference: Using ln(1 + Delta T / T_0) approx Delta T / T_0, we obtain P V = N k T_0.

parts.question: Find the heat capacity of the star at constant volume C_v in term of M and at constant pressure C_p expressed in C_v and T
parts.reference: C_v = (dM/dT)_V * c^2. C_p = C_v + P (dV/dT). Obtain C_p = C_v + N k / ln(T/T_0) * (1 - (T - T_0)/(T ln(T/T_0))).

parts.question: Find the heat produced by the isobaric process if the initial temperature and the final temperature are T_i and T_f, respectively.
parts.reference: Q_H = C_v (T_i - T_f) + N k ((T_f - T_0)/ln(T_f/T_0) - (T_i - T_0)/ln(T_i/T_0)).

parts.question: Suppose there is an observer far away from the star. Using information from part c., estimate the distance of the observer from the star.
parts.reference: Estimation based on observer distance and radiation flux.

parts.question: If the sunlight is monochromatic with frequency 5 * 10^14 Hz, estimate the number of photons radiated by the Sun per second.
Calculate the heat capacity C_v of the Sun assuming its surface temperature varies from 5500 K to 6000 K in one second.
